name: search-cli-phrases
title: search-cli-phrases: the search.mjs command line surface — index, query (quoted or not), stats, and exit codes
interface:
Executable `search.mjs` at the project root, an ES module with zero runtime dependencies.
Successor to the deprecated `search-cli`: every behaviour of that statement still holds, plus quoted phrase queries.
It is the composition layer only: it parses argv, resolves `./index` against process.cwd(),
and delegates to corpus-reader, text-analyzer, positional-index, phrase-matching and bm25-ranking.
No parsing, tokenizing, encoding, matching or scoring logic may be duplicated here.

  index <docs.jsonl>  reads the corpus, builds and writes the index, exits 0 even when
                      lines were skipped; stores the document and skipped counts in the
                      index so later commands need not re-read the corpus.
  query "<terms>"     joins its arguments with single spaces (an unquoted multi-word query
                      is therefore accepted), tokenizes the result with the shared analyzer, ranks with
                      bm25-ranking, prints up to 10 ids one per line, exits 0. Printing
                      zero lines (no term scores above zero) is success, not an error.
                      A query argument containing a CLOSED double-quoted segment is a phrase
                      query: only documents where that segment's tokens occur adjacent and in
                      order (within a title or within a body) may be printed, still ranked
                      best first and still capped at 10. Several quoted segments must all
                      match. Tokens outside the quotes still contribute to the ranking. A
                      query with no closed quotes behaves exactly as it did before.
  stats               prints exactly one JSON object and a newline:
                      {"docs":N,"skipped":M,"indexBytes":B} where B is the summed byte
                      size of every file under ./index/. Exits 0. Unchanged by quoting.

Failure behaviour, uniform: a message on stderr, an empty stdout, exit code 1 — for no
argument, an unknown command, a command given too few arguments (or extra arguments where it
takes a fixed count: index takes exactly one path, stats takes none), a corpus file
that cannot be read, and `query`/`stats` run before any index exists.
nl_description: The user-facing surface: argument parsing, command dispatch, output formatting and exit codes for search.mjs, including the quoting convention that turns a query into an exact-phrase query. It is deliberately thin — every behaviour it exposes belongs to one of the library contracts — but it owns the contract with the judge: the exact stdout shapes (one id per line; one JSON object), the "index dir lives at ./index relative to the working directory" rule, and the rule that every error path is stderr + exit 1 with stdout untouched. Its gate runs the deprecated search-cli gate too, so the unquoted surface cannot regress.
